title: Managed Environments: the Power Platform governance tier, its licensing condition and its controls
summary: The page's licensing conditions, sharing restrictions, environment-group behaviour and administrative controls are supported by Microsoft documentation. The flagged embedded-credentials navigation is documented, and targeted searches found no published automation for maker guidelines or embedded-credentials sharing.

claims.claim: Managed Environments is enabled or edited through Manage > Environments > environment ellipsis > Enable Managed Environments or Edit Managed Environments > Enable or Save.
claims.quote: Select the ellipsis next to an environment, and then in the menu, select Enable Managed Environments. If the environment is already managed, select Edit Managed Environments.

claims.claim: Managed Environments is a suite of premium Power Platform governance capabilities for administrators managing environments at scale.
claims.quote: Managed environments are a suite of premium capabilities that allow admins to manage Power Platform at scale with more control, less effort, and more insights.

claims.claim: Managed Environments can be used with any environment type.

claims.where: What it is: second paragraph; summary

- Limit sharing

claims.where: What it is: Environment groups; Why it matters
claims.claim: A published group rule is enforced in every member environment.
claims.quote: When a rule is published at the environment group level, it's enforced across every environment within that group.

claims.where: What it is: Environment groups; Risks and limits: Group rules
claims.claim: The corresponding environment setting becomes read-only, preventing local administrators from overriding a published group rule.
claims.quote: This means the corresponding setting or policy becomes locked (read-only) within individual environments, ensuring that local system administrators can't modify or override these centrally defined rules.

claims.where: What it is: Environment groups; Risks and limits; Open questions
claims.claim: Per-environment exceptions to published group rules are not currently supported.
claims.quote: Per-environment exceptions aren't currently supported.

claims.claim: Removing an environment from a group preserves its last applied group configuration.
claims.quote: When an environment is removed, it retains the last applied configuration from the group's rules but becomes unlocked, allowing a local admin to modify it going forward.

claims.claim: Removing an environment from a group unlocks its settings for local administration.
claims.quote: When an environment is removed, it retains the last applied configuration from the group's rules but becomes unlocked, allowing a local admin to modify it going forward.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; What it is: Sharing limits
claims.claim: Sharing limits govern canvas apps, solution-aware cloud flows and agents in managed environments.
claims.quote: If a user tries to share a canvas app, solution-aware cloud flow, or agent that contradicts the sharing rules, they're informed as shown.

claims.where: What it is: Sharing limits; Why it matters
claims.claim: Agent sharing controls govern whether owners and editors may grant Editor permissions.
claims.quote: When selected: Owners and editors can share with any individual as an editor.When not selected: Owners and editors can't share with an individual as an editor.

claims.where: What it is: Sharing limits; Why it matters
claims.claim: Agent sharing controls govern whether owners and editors may grant Viewer permissions.
claims.quote: When selected: Owners and editors can share with any individual as a viewer and any security group.When not selected: Owners and editors can't share with an individual as a viewer, nor can they share with a security group.

claims.claim: Agent sharing controls can prevent sharing with security groups.
claims.quote: If this setting is selected, owners and editors can only share with individuals as viewers. They can't share with a security group.

claims.claim: Agent sharing controls can cap the number of viewers.
claims.quote: If Only share with individuals (no security groups) is selected, you can control the maximum number of viewers with whom an agent can be shared with.

claims.where: What it is: Sharing limits; Why it matters; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Sharing rules are prospective and enforced when users attempt to share.
claims.quote: Sharing rules are enforced when users try to share an app, flow, or agent.

claims.where: What it is: Sharing limits; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Sharing rules do not remove access held before the rules were applied.
claims.quote: This restriction doesn't impact any existing users who already have access to the app, flow, or agent before the application of the sharing rules.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Sharing rules are prospective
claims.claim: An app, flow or agent out of compliance can only be unshared until it complies.
claims.quote: However, if an app, flow, or agent is out of compliance after rules are set, only unsharing is allowed until the app, flow, or agent is compliant with the new rules.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Sharing rules are prospective
claims.claim: Sharing-rule enforcement can take up to an hour after configuration.
claims.quote: After sharing rules are set in the Power Platform admin center, it may take up to an hour for them to start getting enforced.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Dataverse for Teams
claims.claim: In Dataverse for Teams, sharing rules do not affect publishing to the team bound to the environment.
claims.quote: Sharing rules in Dataverse for Teams environments don't affect sharing to a Teams team when you publish an agent to Teams.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Dataverse for Teams
claims.claim: Sharing limits are enforced when sharing with individuals or groups in another team.
claims.quote: However, when a user attempts to share with individuals or groups in a Team other than the one bound to the environment, the sharing limits are enforced.

claims.claim: Untouched group rules remain managed at the individual environment level.
claims.quote: Untouched rules are managed at the environment level.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Joining a group
claims.claim: Joining a group can overwrite local sharing limits, maker welcome content, solution checker, usage insights, backup retention and generative AI settings through published group rules.
claims.quote: If you've published any of the following rules within your environment group, the corresponding settings at the environment level are overridden when added to the group: sharing limits, maker welcome content, solution checker, usage insights, backup retention, and generative AI settings.

claims.claim: Changed group rules need republishing to apply their updates.
claims.quote: Updated rules appear in bold with an asterisk (*) until published. Remember to republish rules to apply changes across environments.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: second paragraph; What to check
claims.claim: Every user running an app in a managed environment is in scope, including users of standard apps.

claims.claim: The Developer Plan does not include the Managed Environments entitlement when users run their assets.
claims.quote: A managed environment isn't included as an entitlement in the Developer Plan when users run their assets.

claims.claim: Microsoft gives 30 days as an example trial-licence restriction.
claims.quote: For example, trial licenses only license users for 30 days.
